title: structured output: constrained decoding backends (CFG / regex / tokenizer edgecases)
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Add a first-class constrained decoding abstraction to support structured-output use cases (CFG grammars, regular-expression constraints) while keeping streaming stability and OpenAI-compatibility intact. Customers want predictable, rule-constrained outputs for tool calls and structured payloads without having to implement brittle post-parsing. This PR introduces a pluggable constrained-decoder backend and addresses tokenizer edgecases that previously caused invisible constraint violations in streaming.

Changes at a glance: implemented a ConstrainedDecoder interface plus two backends (cfg_backend and regex_backend); added token_constraint_utils to bridge character-level constraints to token-level masks; updated the OpenAI compatibility adapter to accept and forward constrained_decoding options; made streaming emit constraint lifecycle events so clients observing partial tokens can react when a constraint becomes impossible; added comprehensive unit, integration and fuzz tests.

Commits (summary): "add ConstrainedDecoder interface and basic plumbing"; "implement CFG backend with Earley-style acceptance checking and incremental parser state"; "implement regex backend with token-aware anchored matching"; "tokenizer: add token_alignment and prefix-anchor handling to avoid split-token mismatches"; "openai_compat: accept constrained_decoding param and translate to internal backend config"; "streaming: add constraint_violation and constraint_state events"; "add tests for tokenizer edgecases and streaming behavior"; "fix race in cache invalidation discovered by CI".

Files touched (high level): core decoding and tokenizer utilities, OpenAI compatibility layer, streaming handler, tests, API docs.

Design notes and constraints:
- API surface: new optional request field "constrained_decoding" (forwarded by OpenAI compatibility layer). Its supported shape in examples: {"backend": "cfg|regex", "mode": "strict|best_effort", "grammar": "<EBNF/PEG string>", "patterns": ["regex1","regex2"], "token_level_constraints": true}. The implementation preserves backward compatibility: if constrained_decoding is absent, default behavior is unchanged.
- Backends: CFG backend supports incrementally checking if a prefix can still lead to a valid derivation and enumerating small completions for scoring; regex backend compiles patterns into token-aware NFAs and supports anchored/non-anchored modes. Both backends expose a fast 'is_possible_prefix' check used by the sampler to mask token logits.
- Tokenizer edgecases: introduced token_alignment utilities that map character ranges to token indices and a prefix-anchor mode that toes the line when constraints start at a character boundary that doesn't align with tokenization. This fixes real-world failure modes where quoted strings, punctuation, or multi-byte characters caused constraints to appear violated mid-stream.
- Streaming compatibility: streaming now emits constraint state updates as structured events so SDKs and clients can surface partial failures immediately (we also added an opt-out boolean to avoid noisy events for some customers).
- OpenAI compatibility: adapter accepts the constrained_decoding param and translates into internal ConstrainedDecoder creation; we kept the OpenAI API signature surface compatible and only extended behavior when the compatibility layer sees the new field.

Testing and CI: initial CI run failed due to a subtle race in the serving cache invalidation used by the cfg_backend tests; fixed by serializing cache invalidation and adding a deterministic test harness. We added unit tests (edge token splits, regex overlaps, back-to-back constraints), fuzz tests across tokenizers (BPE and sentencepiece style), and an end-to-end streaming integration test that verifies both the emitted constraint events and final output respecting grammar anchors.

Review summary:
- Arjun requested stronger tests around tokenization of multi-byte unicode and a clearer public doc of expected errors; author added targeted fuzz cases and an errors table in docs.
- Noah suggested replacing a greedy NFA conversion with a lazy-on-demand matcher to reduce memory for large regex specs; implemented lazy matcher and measured 2.3x lower peak memory on benchmark-lab inputs.
- Sasha flagged potential perf regressions in hot loops; micro-optimized the is_possible_prefix fast path and added a benchmark in perf-canary.

Approvals: Arjun and Noah approved after follow-ups; Sasha gave final approval after perf benchmark. Merge: squash merge into main.

Rollout/migration notes:
- No customer-visible breaking changes when not using constrained_decoding.
- SDKs (python/ts/go) will be updated to expose the param in a follow-up PR that hooks into streaming event decoding.
- Recommend staged rollout: enable backend in a canary region with verbose streaming logs and measure constraint-failure rates for 48h.

Release notes: "Add pluggable constrained decoding backends (CFG and regex) with token-alignment fixes and streaming constraint events; enables reliable structured-output enforcement for function/tool calling and OpenAI-compat workflows."

Known limitations and future work:
- CFG backend currently supports a subset of EBNF constructs (no arbitrary semantic actions) and is intended for structural validation rather than full parsing/treatment of semantics.
- Very large grammars or hundreds of regex patterns still consume memory; we plan a serialized-grammar on-disk loader for dedicated instances.
- SDK ergonomics and examples live in follow-up PRs.

CI summary and health: current CI green on main, unit and integration tests added; perf-canary shows negligible impact on tail latency with token-level masking enabled.
release_notes: Add pluggable constrained decoding backends (CFG + regex) with token-alignment utilities and streaming constraint events. Backward compatible; opt-in via the new constrained_decoding request field. Includes tests and docs.
